doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Best band, and advice to young musicians
summary: Tate calls Basie the best swinging band and advises young players to practice, listen and stay hungry.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: A couple of last questions I would like to ask you. Was the Basie band the best big band there ever was?

Swinging. I thought so. I thought it was. Because it could, it could basically sit right here in this room and swing like a dog, and the room didn’t have to be no bigger than this. And he could keep the band down and be swinging like crazy. And I thought he had, I thought he had about the best swinging band.

One last question I would like to ask you is if you could give a word to the field of music, if you wanted to leave a word behind, a word of wisdom, to younger musicians who would come after you and learn something from you, what would you tell them, about tone, about phrasing, about music, about spirit?

Well I would tell them to practice and listen, don’t think you know it all, always listen because everybody’s got something to say. And keep swinging. I tell them keep trying to blow and always listen, because everybody’s got something to say, and never think you know it all.
So you’ve got to stay hungry.
You’ve got to stay hungry. Yeah. Never know it all.
